interviews.what_early_means: N/A for her niche recruiting but can see how that impacts role in admin, etc - First couple of days
interviews.applying_early_notes: “If I open it today and they apply, I’ll call them right away.” “If they apply in two weeks… I will still call them.”
interviews.high_volume_strategy: Rarely overwhelmed (niche field). If high volume, would first review ATS “qualified” group, then double-check screening questions
interviews.trends: Typical flow = 5–10 qualified candidates per new physician role. Sponsored positions attract slightly more; non-sponsored yield fewer
interviews.additional_comments: Notes disconnect between what candidates tell her vs. what resumes show; resume alignment is crucial. Emphasizes keywords and accredited schools as differentiators. Stresses that even if ATS flags “not qualified,” she still reviews manually

interviews.ats_systems_used: Currently Paylocity; previously Lever, Taleo, iCIMS, Workday, Workable

match_score.detail: Not yet. Paylocity is rolling out AI features, but her team has not been trained on them yet

knockout_questions.detail: Yes — used more frequently recently, especially for eligibility and authorization screening

ats_rejects_on_content.detail: No

interviews.where_they_heard_the_ats_myth: Candidates hear it on LinkedIn or via employee referrals.
interviews.myth_busting_notes: “We hear it all the time… most companies are not going to do that because they don’t want to miss out on somebody qualified.” “When it comes to formatting, really try to keep that simple, like taking the images out so it does not kick it out.”
interviews.advice_beyond_qualifications: Drive and advancement potential stand out. Entry-level candidates with transferable experience can get considered. Resume tips: key skills up top, highlight wins, don’t just paste the job description

applying_early_helps.detail: Yes — especially for urgent or high-volume roles

interviews.what_early_means: Within the first week, ideally first 5 days after posting
interviews.applying_early_notes: “Within the first five days of the openings, that’s usually your best opportunity to get a phone conversation with myself or my team.”
interviews.high_volume_strategy: Team uses divide and conquer after intake calls. Resumes are reviewed collectively to avoid missing qualified candidates. Entry-level roles may hit 800–900 applicants; sometimes she has to pause postings
interviews.trends: High volume particularly for entry-level customer service roles. Hiring managers increasingly review 5–6 candidates before making offers, not just 1–2 as before
interviews.additional_comments: She actively debunks myths with her team and hiring managers. Notes candidates often worry about formatting or images wrongly leading to rejection. Emphasizes networking + clear resume wins as critical

interviews.ats_systems_used: iCIMS (current), trial of Greenhouse, previously Taleo

match_score.detail: Yes — iCIMS and Greenhouse offer it, but not turned on in current org. [name redacted] has used AI/match scoring tools in other contexts, but mainly for sourcing/screening, not rejection

knockout_questions.detail: Yes — iCIMS and Greenhouse offer it, but not turned on in current org. [name redacted] has used AI/match scoring tools in other contexts, but mainly for sourcing/screening, not rejection

ats_rejects_on_content.detail: No — ATS does not reject based on formatting/keywords

interviews.where_they_heard_the_ats_myth: Annoying LinkedIn posts (used to sell resume services) Articles on outlets like MSNBC/Yahoo promoting “beat the ATS” narratives
interviews.myth_busting_notes: “It’s such a false narrative… taking advantage of people with scare tactics.” “The ATS is only going to reject you if you don’t meet position requirements… not because your resume formatting is off.”
interviews.advice_beyond_qualifications: Candidates must be comfortable on video calls and able to present themselves well remotely. Learn to translate hobbies/side skills into resume content (e.g., computer building, race cars → technician skills). Condense resumes: 2 pages max, highlight wins and impact, not just duties

applying_early_helps.detail: Yes — but situational. Timing of day/week matters (e.g., posting on Friday night = less useful). Urges balance over rushing

interviews.what_early_means: Not fixed; suggests apply as soon as you see the job if you’re a good fit
interviews.applying_early_notes: “If you see it, apply right away… but don’t stress if recruiter is in different time zone or schedule.” “Better to take a little more time to hire the right person than rush the wrong one.”
interviews.high_volume_strategy: Example: IT role with 600 applicants - capped posting. Divided work among sourcers to check 3 baseline criteria. All reviews were manual (no AI filtering).
interviews.trends: Marketing roles: very high volume (hundreds). Director-level roles: also many unqualified applicants (e.g., fresh grads applying to director roles). Notes rising mismatch between role requirements and applicant profiles
interviews.additional_comments: Resume should show impact, not just titles (e.g., process improvements, sales increases). Prefers concise, well-laid-out resumes. Networking and direct outreach (LinkedIn) can give candidates an edge.

interviews.ats_systems_used: Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, BrassRing, UltiPro, iCIMS

match_score.detail: No — hasn’t worked with ATS match scoring yet. Notes Greenhouse and Ashby are developing it

knockout_questions.detail: Yes — certifications, work authorization. Not used on every posting, but finds them helpful

ats_rejects_on_content.detail: No

interviews.where_they_heard_the_ats_myth: Seen on LinkedIn (from candidates and some career coaches pushing ATS-compliant resumes)
interviews.myth_busting_notes: “In the ATS I’ve worked with, that has not been the case.” “I see it on LinkedIn… some career coaches wanting to sell ATS versions of resumes, but in reality, it’s not a thing.”
interviews.advice_beyond_qualifications: Show you meet qualifications from job description clearly. Resume content matters most — highlight relevant experience directly tied to posting

applying_early_helps.detail: Neutral — doesn’t guarantee outcome, but “doesn’t hurt.” Encourages applying even if role’s been up for weeks

interviews.what_early_means: Not strict — just apply when you see a role, whether day 1 or 2 weeks in
interviews.applying_early_notes: “Doesn’t hurt… but if you see a role you’re a strong fit for that’s been posted two weeks, I’d still say apply.”
interviews.high_volume_strategy: Pauses/unposts roles when applicant numbers reach several hundred (e.g., 500 for remote finance role). Restarts after clearing backlog. Uses keyword searches to prioritize, but reviews all
interviews.trends: Remote corporate roles (finance analyst) can get hundreds quickly (e.g., 35–40 in a day). Has seen 500+ applicants, sometimes close to 1000, but not the norm
interviews.additional_comments: Strongly emphasizes resume content over formatting. Advises uploading resumes as PDF (to prevent formatting issues when parsed). Glad that recruiters are refuting myths about ATS rejections more actively

interviews.role: VP of human resources (solo HR function)
interviews.ats_systems_used: PeopleSoft, ADP, Paycom, Bullhorn, Excel spreadsheets

match_score.detail: Yes — uses LinkedIn’s skills match (e.g., 3 of 7, 5 of 7). She sorts applicants by number of matches. Not using Paycom ATS for this

knockout_questions.detail: Yes — main one: U.S. residency / visa sponsorship (knocks out ~30%)

ats_rejects_on_content.detail: No formal ATS rejection, but LinkedIn sorting = functional filtering. Resumes with fewer than 4/7 skills are auto-rejected manually

interviews.share_rejected_automatically: 30% rejected via knockout (residency/sponsorship). For skills match: keeps ~25 resumes, prefers at least 5/7 skills. Others quickly rejected
interviews.where_they_heard_the_ats_myth: Hasn’t heard the myth at all
interviews.myth_busting_notes: “No, haven’t heard anything about that.” “I’ll sort it by the number of matches… if we’re looking for seven skills, I want to see at least five of the seven.”
interviews.advice_beyond_qualifications: Apply early, especially for high-volume/nationwide postings. Tailor resume to the role, highlight relevant skills. Multiple resumes for different applications recommended

applying_early_helps.detail: Yes — “first come, first serve” when overwhelmed by volume (mentioned without probing)

interviews.what_early_means: Within the first 3 days
interviews.applying_early_notes: “I hate to say it, but it’s first come, first serve, just because I don’t have time to review that many resumes.”
interviews.high_volume_strategy: For nationwide roles: 500–1,000+ resumes. Reviews first ~50 with strong skills match (5/7 or better). Quickly rejects those with 4/7 or fewer skills
interviews.trends: Applicant volume has spiked in last 6 months. 2 years ago: 150–250 for nationwide roles; now 500–1,000+
interviews.additional_comments: Admits she’s a newbie to AI; wants to invest more in tools to keep up with rising volume.

interviews.ats_systems_used: Phenom, Workday; previously [company name redacted] proprietary system

match_score.detail: Yes — Phenom provides a % fit score. Currently training the AI (thumbs up/down feedback). He says it’s inconsistent: gives high scores to weak candidates and low scores to strong ones. They review all resumes manually, but hope to rely more on AI in future

knockout_questions.detail: Yes — Phenom provides a % fit score. Currently training the AI (thumbs up/down feedback). He says it’s inconsistent: gives high scores to weak candidates and low scores to strong ones. They review all resumes manually, but hope to rely more on AI in future

ats_rejects_on_content.detail: No — Phenom’s AI is supposed to screen for job description criteria, but trust is low, so recruiters don’t rely on it

interviews.where_they_heard_the_ats_myth: He hasn’t heard the myth at all — no press, LinkedIn, or candidate mentions
interviews.advice_beyond_qualifications: Tailor resume with specific keywords from job description. Include both acronyms and full spellings (e.g., SQL and “Structured Query Language”). Make company, job title, and dates clear on page one — don’t make recruiter hunt

applying_early_helps.detail: No — he posts jobs for a fixed 2–3 day window, then reviews everyone together. Timing doesn’t affect chances

interviews.applying_early_notes: “Applying early doesn’t matter… it all goes in the same pool.”
interviews.high_volume_strategy: Opens postings for 2–3 days, then caps at ~150 applicants. Reviews all, communicates with overflow applicants to “keep them warm.” Reposts if needed
interviews.trends: High-volume roles (call center): 200+ applicants in 3 days. Nurse roles: 10–15 applicants in a week. Director roles: 5 applicants in 2 weeks. Could easily hit 500–1000 if postings left open longer
interviews.additional_comments: Focus on candidate experience — limits posting time to avoid overwhelming applicants. Stresses clarity and keywords on resumes as biggest differentiators

interviews.ats_systems_used: Bullhorn, Taleo, Workday, Microsoft 365 internal, integrating Greenhouse (launch Jan next year)

match_score.detail: Yes — Workday and Greenhouse provide % match. He uses it as a guideline only: Helps organize when many resumes flood in the first week. Looks at keywords, skills, salary range, and location. Still manually reviews for red flags (e.g., job hopping)

knockout_questions.detail: Yes — especially work authorization and sponsorship eligibility (more common in his past tech/finance roles than current construction roles)

ats_rejects_on_content.detail: No — does not configure auto-rejection. “It’s a dangerous space… don’t want to reject referrals without review.”

interviews.where_they_heard_the_ats_myth: Hasn’t heard the “ATS rejection” myth directly. Instead, he’s heard about ghost job postings being created for tax benefits
interviews.myth_busting_notes: Hasn’t heard the “ATS rejection” myth directly. Instead, he’s heard about ghost job postings being created for tax benefits
interviews.advice_beyond_qualifications: Recruiters prefer clean, well-structured resumes (job titles, dates, responsibilities clear). Summaries should explain day-to-day responsibilities. Keywords still important for scanning

applying_early_helps.detail: Yes — especially for high-demand roles. Recruiters often want jobs filled “yesterday”

interviews.what_early_means: Within 24–48 hours of posting
interviews.applying_early_notes: “Earlier people get in… especially if it’s a popular role, like project manager.”
interviews.high_volume_strategy: Uses keywords, location, and salary filters to narrow. Example: project manager role = 100 applicants within 5 days. Admin roles = several hundred applicants; occasionally close to 1,000 if left open
interviews.trends: Strong job market in construction → applicant volume rising last 2–3 years. Typical: 40–80 applicants per week → 200+ over 2–3 weeks. Admin roles can hit several hundred; 1000 if unmanaged
interviews.additional_comments: Notes recruiting has shifted a lot in last 5–6 years, mostly positively. AI tools helpful for organizing, but human judgment still essential

interviews.ats_systems_used: Workday; previously Salesforce CRM + custom homegrown system

match_score.detail: Yes — uses Beamery (connected with Workday) which provides a match score. She says it’s not very accurate and she doesn’t rely on it; instead, she manually reviews applications

knockout_questions.detail: Yes — certifications, and location requirements (knocks out if not in correct on-site/hybrid area)

ats_rejects_on_content.detail: No — all resumes manually reviewed

interviews.where_they_heard_the_ats_myth: Heard mostly from LinkedIn posts and also personal candidate experience (instant rejections at other companies)
interviews.myth_busting_notes: “Sometimes the ATS may not catch all the specifics I’m looking for, so I review all applications myself.” “I’ve applied places and got a rejection right away — there’s no way someone reviewed it. That’s probably why people think it’s automatic rejection.”
interviews.advice_beyond_qualifications: Avoid generic resumes — show impact and specifics (e.g., quota, book of business, scope of responsibilities). Tailor resume to the actual posting; don’t reuse from another job

applying_early_helps.detail: Yes — especially since postings may close early when application numbers get too high

interviews.what_early_means: Within the first couple of hours to 1–3 days. After a month, usually too late since interviews already underway
interviews.applying_early_notes: “Within the first couple hours.” “If a posting’s been up a month, nine times out of ten we’re already well into the interview process.”
interviews.high_volume_strategy: Prioritizes internals, referrals, and previous workers first. Reviews 50–100+ applications daily. If overwhelmed (e.g., 1300 apps), pauses job to “do maintenance” before reopening
interviews.trends: Large company postings = hundreds to 1300+ applicants. Of those, only 15–20% are qualified. For more specialized roles: ~15–20 applicants per day
interviews.additional_comments: Recommends bolding certifications and key requirements so recruiters can spot them quickly. Notes many applicants apply without qualifications out of desperation.

interviews.ats_systems_used: Jobvite, iCIMS

match_score.detail: No — says neither ATS provides a reliable match score; his team reviews all applications manually

knockout_questions.detail: Yes — primarily visa sponsorship eligibility (some roles allow sponsorship, others do not)

ats_rejects_on_content.detail: No — resumes are not auto-rejected for formatting, missing keywords, or listed skills

interviews.where_they_heard_the_ats_myth: Heard from candidates on social media, especially during layoffs — frustration from applying widely with no responses
interviews.myth_busting_notes: “We’re going through each and every application ourselves.” “I’ve heard it as a perception, but haven’t seen it firsthand.”
interviews.advice_beyond_qualifications: -Include facts and figures: scale of work, complexity, metrics (# recruited, team size, results). -Bullet points preferred over paragraphs for quick scanning

applying_early_helps.detail: Yes — strongly believes applying early improves chances

interviews.what_early_means: Within the first week (ideally within first 10–30 resumes reviewed)
interviews.applying_early_notes: “We can build out a pretty deep pipeline in the first 10, 20, 30 resumes we see.” “Those people that apply later just don’t get seen because the req closes.”
interviews.high_volume_strategy: -Reviews resumes manually (20–30 seconds each). -Uses keyword search (e.g., Golang) to help scanning. -May take postings down after ~200 applicants to catch up
interviews.trends: -High-volume roles (e.g., data analyst) = 400–500 resumes in a week. -Recruiter role in Brazil = 250 resumes in a week. -Niche/high-level roles (e.g., Workday consultant) = much fewer. -Uptick in applicant numbers since late 2023, continuing in 2024–25
interviews.additional_comments: -Believes resume clarity (bullet points, numbers, scale of work) makes the biggest difference. -Candidate market is highly competitive; early applicants benefit most
